risks: extract_literals | medium | line_of uses binary search on line starts; correctness depends on starts list being built correctly (starts includes position 0 and positions after each newline). | Verify with a test that includes empty lines and trailing newline.

_COMPILED | low | Compilation uses re.MULTILINE flag; some patterns (e.g., _MAKE) rely on ^ to match start of line, which requires MULTILINE. This is correct but implicit. | Confirm that all patterns expecting line-start anchors work with MULTILINE.

extract_literals | medium | Deduplication key is (relation, raw, line); if the same literal appears on the same line (e.g., in a multiline string), only one is kept. This may miss genuine duplicates. | Decide if line-based dedup is intended or if position-based dedup is safer.
extract_literals | low | MAX_LITERALS_PER_FILE is referenced but not defined in this chunk; extraction may silently truncate. | Define or verify MAX_LITERALS_PER_FILE is set appropriately.

observations.what: MAX_LITERALS_PER_FILE is referenced but not defined in this chunk; it may be defined elsewhere or missing.
line_of function uses binary search on starts list; correctness depends on starts being built correctly (includes position 0 and positions after each newline).
Deduplication key includes line number; if multiple matches on same line with same relation and raw, only first is kept. This may lose information.
Shell redirect patterns require file extension of 1-8 alphanumeric characters; files without extension are ignored.
Makefile pattern uses ^ to match start of line; with re.MULTILINE this works. But the pattern may match comments or variables incorrectly.
